name: Cognex Corporation
fiscal_year_note: Fiscal year = calendar year (ends Dec 31); fiscal quarters end on a Sunday near calendar quarter-end (Q1 2026 ended Apr 5, 2026; Q2 2026 ended Jul 5, 2026). US GAAP. Listed long before 2020, so listing_date is null. Q3 2026 results due Wed Nov 4, 2026 after the close (call Nov 5, 8:30am ET).

latest_period.label: Q2 FY2026 (quarter ended Jul 5, 2026; roughly Apr-Jun 2026)

guidance: Q3 2026 (issued Aug 5, 2026): revenue $300-320M (~12% YoY at midpoint; ~17% excluding a $13M one-time benefit in Q3 2025), adjusted EBITDA margin 32-35%, adjusted diluted EPS $0.50-0.54. FY2026: revenue $1,130-1,150M (~15% growth at midpoint), adjusted EBITDA margin 29-31%, adjusted EPS $1.64-1.68 (includes ~$0.11 of investment income). Cost program: ~$35M of annualized net cost reductions by end-2026 (low end of the $35-40M target set in Feb 2026). End-market outlook raised in Aug 2026: semiconductor, electronics and packaging double-digit growth in 2026; logistics high-single-digit; automotive roughly flat. Through-cycle framework (June 2025 Investor Day): 13-14% revenue CAGR including ~3% from M&A, 20-30% adjusted EBITDA margin, >100% FCF conversion, double the ~30,000-customer base within five years. RealSense (close expected Q4 2026) projects $80-90M of 2026 revenue. Q3 consensus revenue ~$313M (Trefis).
unit_volumes: Cognex does not disclose unit shipments. Customer metrics: >30,000 customers; ~9,000 new customer accounts added in 2025 (about 3x the prior-year pace); >4,500 new customers added in H1 2026; OneVision AI platform used by 'hundreds' of customers (Aug 2026).

physical_ai_exposure.description: Core business is AI-enabled machine vision (2D/3D smart cameras, barcode/ID readers, deep-learning inspection) sold into factory and logistics automation. That is the perception layer of automation, so nearly all revenue is automation-linked, but it is mostly fixed-camera inspection and ID rather than robot-mounted perception. The 7% is my pro-forma estimate of direct robotic-perception revenue after the RealSense deal (~$85M midpoint of RealSense's projected 2026 revenue vs ~$1.14B Cognex FY2026 guide midpoint). Cognex does not disclose revenue from its existing vision-guided-robotics products.
physical_ai_exposure.optionality_notes: RealSense (spun out of Intel in 2025) depth cameras serve fixed robot arms, AMRs, quadrupeds and humanoids. Cognex sizes robotic perception at ~$600M today, growing >25%/yr to ~$1.6B by 2030, and pitches a 'full-stack visual intelligence platform for Physical AI'. Other AI levers: OneVision cloud training and deployment, edge-learning and transformer models (~20M parameters running at ~8W on embedded hardware), the SLX AI logistics system, In-Sight L38 3D, and data-center supply-chain inspection (low-single-digit % of revenue, +30% YoY in Q2 2026).

cost_and_supply_chain_notes: Most hardware is assembled by contract manufacturers in Indonesia and Malaysia; in-house optical-component plants in Shenzhen (China) and Bac Ninh (Vietnam, from Moritex); distribution centers in Cork (Ireland), Southborough (MA) and Singapore. Key inputs are image sensors, processors and memory: rising memory prices are expected to cost ~75 bps of gross margin in Q3 2026 (possibly into Q4), which management plans to offset with price increases. US tariffs on some Chinese-sourced components raised costs but were 'not material' (FY2025 10-K), and tariff refunds were not a material factor in 2026 margins. A ~71% gross margin cushions input-cost swings. Cognex does not make actuators, so rare-earth magnets and reducers are not key inputs (my assessment).
regulatory_notes: US export controls have reduced revenue from China-based customers (immaterial to date per the 10-K). Greater China was 16% of FY2025 revenue, so US-China tariffs and trade measures matter. The RealSense acquisition needs regulatory clearance (close expected Q4 2026), and RealSense will spin out its facial-authentication line before closing. No US government list designations. The 10-K says one customer has at times represented a material portion of total revenue.
key_drivers: Logistics automation: 10 straight quarters of double-digit growth through Q2 2026, driven by large e-commerce customers; FY2026 logistics outlook raised to high-single-digit growth.
Semiconductor and electronics upcycle tied to AI infrastructure: both guided to double-digit growth in 2026; Greater China revenue +42% (constant currency) and Other Asia +14% in Q2 2026.

Restructuring-driven margins: adjusted gross margin 71.5% (+350 bps YoY) and adjusted EBITDA margin 32.2% in Q2 2026; FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guide of 29-31% vs a 20-30% through-cycle target; ~$35M of annualized cost savings by end-2026.
AI product cycle: OneVision generally available with hundreds of customers; In-Sight 2800/L38/3900/6900, SLX, and the In-Sight 1750 wafer reader (Sep 2026); ~9,000 new customers in 2025.
Entry into robotic perception through RealSense ($500M; $80-90M 2026 revenue, >50% growth) in a ~$600M market growing >25%/yr.

Balance sheet and capital returns: $755M of cash and investments and no debt before RealSense; $151M of buybacks in 2025 and $99M in Q1 2026; $500M added to the authorization in Feb 2026; $0.085 quarterly dividend.
Earnings momentum: FY2026 adjusted EPS guide of $1.64-1.68 vs $1.02 in FY2025 (~+63%).
key_risks: Automotive weakness, especially in Europe: automotive revenue fell at a high-single-digit rate in Q2 2026 and Europe revenue fell 15%.
Logistics deceleration and customer concentration: management expects logistics growth to moderate in H2 2026, and one customer has at times been a material share of revenue.

High expectations: Q3 2025 included a $13M one-time benefit, which makes for a tough Q3 comparison; Q2 2026 revenue slightly missed consensus and the stock fell ~5%; shares trade at ~53x trailing and ~31x forward earnings.
Input costs: memory price inflation is a ~75 bps gross-margin headwind in Q3 2026.
RealSense execution: ~$500M of cash (about two-thirds of cash and investments) plus ~$106M of retention cash and RSUs, integration risk, and an early-stage robotics-perception market.
China and export-control exposure (Greater China was 16% of FY2025 revenue) and cyclical factory-automation capex.
Volatility: 52-week range $34.60-$72.88; shares are ~24% below the 52-week high.

recent_events.event: Investor Day: through-cycle targets of 13-14% revenue CAGR (incl. ~3% M&A), 20-30% adjusted EBITDA margin and >100% FCF conversion; goal to double ~30,000 customers in five years; showcased AI tools (OneVision, edge learning, In-Sight L38 3D, DataMan 290).

Q3 2025: revenue $277M (+18%; +13% excluding a one-time $13M commercial-partnership benefit), adjusted EPS $0.33 (beat). The Q4 guide of $230-245M revenue and $0.19-0.24 adjusted EPS was read as soft.
recent_events.stock_reaction: approx. -12% (from $47.44 before the report to $41.80, per StockStory; my calculation)

recent_events.event: Q4 2025: revenue $252M (+10%); FY2025 revenue $994M (+9%) and adjusted EPS $1.02 (+38%); Q1 2026 guide of $235-255M with a 19-22% adjusted EBITDA margin; $500M buyback authorization increase; exiting ~$22M of non-core revenue; additional $35-40M of annualized cost cuts targeted by end-2026.
recent_events.stock_reaction: +39% intraday on Feb 12 to a 52-week high of $59.88 (Motley Fool); ~+36% vs the $43.03 pre-earnings price (StockStory)

recent_events.event: Q1 2026: revenue $268M (+24%, vs ~$246M consensus), adjusted EPS $0.34 (+113%), GAAP operating margin 22.3%; $99M of buybacks; Q2 guide $280-300M.

Q2 2026: record revenue of $291M (+17%), slightly below ~$292-293M consensus; adjusted EPS $0.45 (vs $0.42 consensus); adjusted EBITDA margin 32.2%; FY2026 guide of $1.13-1.15B revenue and $1.64-1.68 adjusted EPS. Management flagged moderating logistics growth in H2 and a ~75 bps memory-cost headwind in Q3.
recent_events.stock_reaction: -5.4% post-earnings (AllInvestView); about -9.8% over the following month (Zacks, Sep 4)

recent_events.event: Agreed to acquire RealSense for ~$500M in cash plus a $56.5M cash retention plan and ~$50M of RSUs. RealSense projects $80-90M of 2026 revenue (>50% growth); close expected Q4 2026; framed as Cognex's entry into robotic perception and physical AI.
recent_events.stock_reaction: +0.5% premarket to $62.31 (RTT/Nasdaq) but closed at $58.97, roughly -5% on the day (my calculation)

recent_events.event: Launched the In-Sight 1750 wafer reader for semiconductor manufacturers.

Analyst moves from late Sep to mid-Oct: Baird cut its target to $70 (Neutral), Truist cut to $74 (Hold), and Barclays raised to $85 (Overweight, ~Oct 13). Shares fell from $61.82 (Oct 12 close) to $53.99 (Oct 16).
recent_events.stock_reaction: -12.7% over Oct 13-16 (my calculation from stockanalysis closes); cause not identified in sources reviewed

recent_events.event: Set the Q3 2026 report for Nov 4, 2026 after the close; consensus revenue ~$313M.

notes: Estimates and caveats: (1) total_debt = 0 because Cognex reports no borrowings; stockanalysis lists ~$72M of 'debt', likely lease liabilities. (2) cash_burn_annual = 0 because the company is free-cash-flow positive (FY2025 FCF $237M; TTM FCF ~$268M per stockanalysis). (3) ev_sales_forward 7.2 is my calculation: EV of ~$8.6B ($9.36B market cap minus $0.755B cash and investments) divided by ~$1.19B forward revenue, the figure implied by stockanalysis's forward P/S of 7.84 (Oct 23 data). Stockanalysis's own EV of $9.01B excludes $351M of non-current investments. Forward P/E 31.0 and P/S 8.6 are stockanalysis figures. (4) The 7% physical_ai_exposure figure is my pro-forma estimate including RealSense. (5) The 10-K discloses only a combined ~85% share for logistics, packaging, consumer electronics and automotive; the 15% remainder is implied. Geo mix is FY2025 from the 10-K. (6) Q2 2026 adjusted (non-GAAP) gross margin was 71.5% and adjusted operating margin 30.7%; latest_period uses GAAP figures. (7) Stock reactions marked 'my calculation' come from stockanalysis closing prices or prices quoted in articles; the RealSense-day move assumes the ~$61.99 Sep 21 close implied by the premarket quote. (8) Price is the Oct 26, 2026 close (after-hours $56.24). Consensus target $79.37 (20 analysts, 'Buy'). (9) The Investor Day date comes from the company's announcement title. (10) The search budget ran out during research, so a few items are marked 'not found'.
